name: More machines than jobs
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 5)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
why: True: the busiest machine has at most 4/3 of the best possible, 5. One job per machine.

name: In the given order is not enough
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 3)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
why: True: the busiest machine has at most 4/3 of the best possible, 3. Placing the jobs in the given order onto the least loaded machine ends with loads 2, 2, 2 and then 5 for the last job. Taking the longest job first gives 3, 3, 3.

name: Two machines
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 6)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
why: True: the busiest machine has at most 4/3 of the best possible, 6. Longest first gives 7 against the best 6 (3 + 3 and 2 + 2 + 2): not the best, but within 4/3.

name: Graham's example
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 9)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
why: True: the busiest machine has at most 4/3 of the best possible, 9. Longest first gives 11 against the best 9 (5 + 4, 5 + 4, 3 + 3 + 3): within 4/3, as the guarantee promises.

name: Random jobs
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 78)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
why: True: the busiest machine has at most 4/3 of the best possible, 78. Checked against the best of all 3⁸ assignments.

name: Equal jobs
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 21)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
why: True: the busiest machine has at most 4/3 of the best possible, 21. Three machines get 3 jobs and one gets 1, or 3, 3, 2, 2: the busiest has 21.

name: 200,000 jobs on 10,000 machines
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 1000000)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
show: 10,000 machines; jobs made by cutting 10,000 blocks of 1,000,000 into about 20 pieces each, so the best possible is 1,000,000
why: Looking through all 10,000 machines for the least loaded one, for each of 200,000 jobs, is 2 × 10⁹ steps: too slow, even with min() running in C. A heap of machines by load does it in O(n log m).

name: Few machines, many jobs
expr: (lambda s: s if isinstance(s, str) else 3 * s <= 4 * 1000000)(makespan(args[0], args[1], schedule(list(args[0]), args[1])))
show: 4 machines; jobs made by cutting 4 blocks of 1,000,000 into about 5000 pieces each, so the best possible is 1,000,000
